reviews.reasons: The no-plan conclusion itself is right: no opening has a price any buyer is shown paying (the only website price evidence is WebFX's $100-$5,000 generic range, which I verified fails scope), no close rate, no current buying signal and no confirmed fulfiller, and the decisive links named (OFFER_AND_PRICE, CONVERSION) are the ones the evidence decides; nothing is misstated as a constraint. But the resolution the owner would act on does not work as written: passing its test at its threshold does not carry the target. The threshold is 3 deposits from 350 contacts (0.86%), which needs ~1,500 contacts for 12 sales; at the stated 50 emails a day from the owner's own mailbox, 350 contacts take to day 7 and the remaining ~1,150 take another 23 days, i.e. the last contact goes out about day 30, leaving no time for the 5-day builds or for the 50% balances to be collected inside the 30-day window. So the test either needs a channel throughput that is evidenced to reach ~1,500 contacts by about day 15, or a pass threshold high enough that the measured rate reaches 12 sales from the contacts actually reachable in time (e.g. ~12 sales from ~700 contacts by day 15 = ~1.7%), or the resolution should say plainly that even passing it does not reach $12,000 in 30 days.
findings: Throughput arithmetic: 12 sales / 0.86% = ~1,400-1,500 contacts; 50/day x 30 days = 1,500 contacts, finishing on day 30 - no time to build (5 days) and collect the balance.

'No warmup needed' for 50 cold emails a day from the owner's existing personal mailbox is not sourced; only the 2-week warmup for new inboxes is. The test's own channel capacity and deliverability is therefore an unknown, and the owner's hours to send and handle 50 personal emails a day are not stated (ownerHoursPerWeek is null).
Collected-cash ledger: with 50% deposits, the $12,000 needs all 12 balances collected by day 30, not just deposits; the proof should be stated in collected cash.
Capital: 12 builds x ~$250 = ~$3,000 exceeds the $2,500 cap unless each is paid from its own deposit; the resolution says so, which is correct, but the per-build order must wait for its deposit.

DataAnnotation exclusion basis: 'a wage, not a price a buyer pays' is not a valid exclusion (a payer paying for delivered work is still a buyer). The opening fails on its own record instead: 240-480 owner hours in 30 days against unstated owner hours, and work availability not guaranteed by the payer's FAQ. State that basis.
Freelancer.com alternative correctly not adopted: price and award rate unestablished, 17-490 competing bids.

reviews.reasons: NO_PLAN remains right (no price any buyer is shown paying, no close rate, no demand signal, no confirmed fulfiller; decisive links CONVERSION and OFFER_AND_PRICE; nothing called a constraint), and the recommended test now carries the target if it passes at its threshold. Recomputed: 5 deposits of 350 = 1.43%; 50/day to day 17 = 850 contacts; 1.43% x 850 = ~12 sales = $12,000; last contacts on day 17 leave ~1-3 days to pay a deposit, 5 days to build (~day 22-25) and balances collected by ~day 25-27 inside 30. Capital: each ~$250 build is ordered only after its own $500 deposit clears, so cash never goes negative and the $2,500 cap is never touched. Proof is in collected cash ($2,500 by day 8). Fulfilment is checked by written designer quotes before any order is taken. Mailbox deliverability is now an UNKNOWN measured in the test with a 3% bounce stop; owner hours stated (~1.5 h/day; no hours ceiling in the contract). DataAnnotation exclusion now rests on its own record (240-480 owner hours, availability not guaranteed).
findings: Pass threshold sits right at the edge: 1.43% x 850 = 12.1 sales, so any shortfall in contacts sent (bounces, days missed) misses $12,000; the continue rule should re-check the cumulative rate on ~day 12.
Excluded DataAnnotation reason still adds 'Brain also classes it as owner wage'; the stated record-based reason is what carries the exclusion.
Ledger is empty by design (NO_PLAN); trace shows $0 spent and $2,500 untouched.

Its Instantly channel cannot even start at volume in time: new inboxes need at least 2 weeks of warmup before campaigns. Freelancer.com requests clear at ~$140-$450 against 17-490 bids (35 wins needed), and DataAnnotation is a wage, not a sale.

alternatives.title: Bid on Freelancer.com website requests, Fiverr designer fulfils
alternatives.why: Budgets ~INR 12,500-37,500 (~$140-$420) with 17-490 competing bids; 35 awards and milestone releases in 30 days is not established.

alternatives.title: Hourly AI-training work on DataAnnotation
alternatives.why: Excluded: 240-480 owner hours in 30 days from a payer that does not guarantee work.

steps.label: Before any offer: message 3 Fiverr WordPress designers for written quotes (price, 5-page scope, delivery days, capacity for 12 sites in 3 weeks); proceed only with one confirming <= $300 and <= 5 days

Experiment: owner sends ~50/day plain emails from his existing mailbox to 350 local service businesses with no website, offering a $1,000 5-page site, 50% deposit (days 1-7); bounces and spam placement are logged as the channel's own measurement

Decide on day 8: a confirmed designer and >= 5 paid $500 deposits ($2,500 collected) from 350 contacts -> continue to ~500 more contacts by day 17 (850 total), order each build only after its own deposit, collect balances by day 25; fewer -> stop

noPlan.decisiveGap: No buyer is shown paying ~$1,000 for a cold-emailed local-business website, and no close rate is measured; 12 such sales in 30 days (and a warmed cold-email channel, which itself needs 2+ weeks) is therefore not established.
noPlan.resolution: Day 0-1 ($0): get written quotes from 3 Fiverr WordPress designers (<= $300/site, <= 5 days, capacity for 12 sites in 3 weeks) - this measures FULFILMENT before any order is taken. Days 1-7 ($0, ~1.5 owner hours/day): from the owner's existing mailbox email 350 local service businesses without a website, $1,000 site, 50% deposit; log bounces and spam placement (its deliverability at 50/day is itself unmeasured). Proof, in collected cash: a confirmed designer and >= 5 paid $500 deposits ($2,500 collected) by day 8 = 1.4%, the rate at which the ~850 contacts reachable at 50/day by day 17 give 12 sales, leaving 5 days to build and balances collected by ~day 25. Continue: email ~500 more by day 17; order each build only after its own deposit has cleared (so 12 x ~$250 never exceeds the $2,500 cap at once). Stop: no designer confirms, fewer than 5 deposits by day 8, bounce rate over 3%, or replies rejecting the price. Even a 0.86% rate (3 of 350) would not reach $12,000 inside 30 days.

answers.finding: Throughput arithmetic: 0.86% needs ~1,500 contacts, finishing day 30
answers.resolution: Accepted. Pass threshold raised to >= 5 deposits of 350 (1.4%), so 12 sales come from the ~850 contacts reachable by day 17, builds finish by ~day 22 and balances are collected by ~day 25; the resolution now says a 0.86% rate would not reach the target.

answers.finding: Proof should be stated in collected cash
answers.resolution: Accepted. Proof is now >= $2,500 collected (5 paid $500 deposits) by day 8, and continuation requires all 12 balances collected by ~day 25.

excluded.why: Fails on its own record: $12,000 at the published $25-$50/h needs 240-480 owner hours in 30 days, and the payer's FAQ says work availability depends on demand and performance, so the volume is not available to plan on (Brain also classes it as owner wage rather than a sale).

disagreements.reason: Its revenueRange is verified EVIDENCE quoting the payer's FAQ ('Starting at $25-$50 per hour'); the opening is excluded as a wage, not for want of a rate.
$0 cost and $0 capital against a published hourly rate.

review.reasons: NO_PLAN remains right (no price any buyer is shown paying, no close rate, no demand signal, no confirmed fulfiller; decisive links CONVERSION and OFFER_AND_PRICE; nothing called a constraint), and the recommended test now carries the target if it passes at its threshold. Recomputed: 5 deposits of 350 = 1.43%; 50/day to day 17 = 850 contacts; 1.43% x 850 = ~12 sales = $12,000; last contacts on day 17 leave ~1-3 days to pay a deposit, 5 days to build (~day 22-25) and balances collected by ~day 25-27 inside 30. Capital: each ~$250 build is ordered only after its own $500 deposit clears, so cash never goes negative and the $2,500 cap is never touched. Proof is in collected cash ($2,500 by day 8). Fulfilment is checked by written designer quotes before any order is taken. Mailbox deliverability is now an UNKNOWN measured in the test with a 3% bounce stop; owner hours stated (~1.5 h/day; no hours ceiling in the contract). DataAnnotation exclusion now rests on its own record (240-480 owner hours, availability not guaranteed).
findings: Pass threshold sits right at the edge: 1.43% x 850 = 12.1 sales, so any shortfall in contacts sent (bounces, days missed) misses $12,000; the continue rule should re-check the cumulative rate on ~day 12.
Excluded DataAnnotation reason still adds 'Brain also classes it as owner wage'; the stated record-based reason is what carries the exclusion.
Ledger is empty by design (NO_PLAN); trace shows $0 spent and $2,500 untouched.

basis.intent: Turn $2,500 into at least $12,000 of collected cash within 30 days. Any industry is fine.
